mainTopic: The paid שטר dispute, and the שיעור for carrying hide whether raw or processed
overview: This amud opens with the last words of an earlier explanation of the dispute between the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה about carrying a שטר that was already paid. רבא explains the dispute as a question of whether we write a שובר, and רב אשי says the paid note is useful to show a second lender. The גמרא then turns to the line in the משנה about hide. רבא asks רב נחמן about the שיעור for carrying hide, tanning it, carrying it in order to tan it, and carrying it with no plan to tan it. Each time רב נחמן answers 'לא שנא': enough to make a קמיע. The גמרא proves this from a משנה about wool, where material meant to be spun is measured like spun thread. רבא challenges this ruling from dyes, seeds and clay, and each challenge is answered with the idea of אין אדם טורח: people do not bother preparing such a tiny amount. Two more challenges follow, from עולא's three stages of hide and from a תוספתא that gives hide a measure of five by five. The גמרא answers that those sources refer to special kinds of hide, wet fresh hide and קורטובלא.

steps.title: End of the earlier explanation: until the borrower says 'I paid' or 'I did not pay'
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of an earlier explanation of the dispute about carrying a paid שטר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until the borrower says, 'I paid' or 'I did not pay.'
steps.whatsHappening: These are the last words of an explanation the גמרא was already in the middle of. It frames the dispute around what happens when the לוה claims 'I paid.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this earlier approach, the argument is about whether a שטר the borrower admits writing still needs קיום. If it does need קיום and there are no witnesses, the paid note is worthless, so carrying it is not a real carrying. If it does not need קיום, the note still has value.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I paid' — the borrower's claim that he already repaid the loan
A written legal document, here a loan note

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new statement. It is the tail end of an explanation that began on the previous amud, so it only makes sense together with that earlier text.

phrases.english: Until the borrower says
phrases.notes: This picks up an explanation that started on the previous amud.

phrases.english: 'I paid' or 'I did not pay.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an explanation earlier
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The value of a paid note depends on what happens when the borrower claims he paid, which ties into the question of קיום שטרות.

steps.title: רבא: everyone agrees the note needs ratification; the dispute is about writing a receipt
steps.stepSummary: רבא moves the dispute away from קיום שטרות and explains it as a dispute about whether we write a שובר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Everyone agrees that when a borrower admits he wrote a note, the lender must still get it ratified. Here they argue about whether we write a receipt. The תנא קמא holds that we write a receipt, and רבי יהודה holds that we do not write a receipt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different explanation of the dispute. In his view, both sides agree about קיום, and they disagree about whether a שובר is written when a loan is repaid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we write a שובר, the borrower is protected by the receipt. The lender does not have to give the old note back, so when he carries it he has no need for it. If we do not write a שובר, the lender must give the note back to the borrower, so he does need it, and רבי יהודה holds he is חייב for carrying it.

keyTerms.meaning: One who admits that he wrote the document
To ratify it in בית דין through the witnesses' signatures
A receipt confirming that a debt was paid
The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the same ברייתא can be explained through completely different legal questions: קיום שטרות in one approach, and כותבין שובר in רבא's approach.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Everyone agrees that one who admits a note that he wrote —
it must be ratified,
and here they disagree about whether we write a receipt:
the first Tanna holds we write a receipt,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר אֵין כּוֹתְבִין שׁוֹבָר.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehuda holds we do not write a receipt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the earlier framing (a dispute about קיום) and offers a new framing
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute between the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה is about כותבין שובר, not about קיום שטרות.

steps.title: רב אשי: he needs the paid note to show a second lender
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains why רבי יהודה holds one is liable: the paid note proves that the borrower pays his debts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: He is liable because he needs to show the note to a second lender, saying to him: 'Look, I am a man who pays back.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a third explanation. The paid note is useful to the borrower as proof of his good credit when he wants a new loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying on שבת is only a מלאכה when the object has some real use. רב אשי finds the use in the paid note itself: it shows a new lender that this borrower is trustworthy. That is why רבי יהודה makes him חייב.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three explanations of the dispute about a paid שטר: the earlier one (about קיום), רבא's (about כותבין שובר), and רב אשי's (it is useful to show a second lender).

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
because he needs to show it
to a second lender,
for he says to him:
Look, I am a man who repays.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לְהַרְאוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers another way to explain רבי יהודה's ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A paid note has value because the borrower can show it to a new lender as proof that he repays.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: hide, enough to make an amulet
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about the measure for carrying hide, opening a new topic.
steps.simpleTranslation: Hide: enough to make an amulet, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new discussion. It quotes the line in the משנה about animal hide so it can ask questions about it next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives the שיעור for carrying hide as the amount needed for a קמיע. The questions that follow ask whether this same measure applies in other situations involving hide.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc. — short for וְכוּלֵּיהּ, the rest of the quote

phrases.english: Hide — enough to make, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic; moves from the paid שטר to hide
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The measure for carrying hide is enough to make a קמיע.

steps.title: רבא asks רב נחמן: how much hide makes one liable for carrying?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב נחמן what the measure is for carrying hide.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked רב נחמן: One who carries out hide, how much does he need to carry?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a series of questions about hide. He starts with the basic question about carrying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This first question has a known answer in the משנה. It lays the groundwork so that רבא can ask harder follow-up questions next.

keyTerms.meaning: One who carries out from one domain to another

phrases.english: Rava asked Rav Nachman:
One who carries out hide — how much?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the משנה just quoted

steps.title: רב נחמן: as the משנה says, enough for an amulet
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers from the משנה: enough hide to make a קמיע.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: As we learned in the משנה: hide, enough to make an amulet.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the first question by quoting the משנה directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic measure is now fixed: a piece of hide big enough for a קמיע. All of the following questions will be compared to this measure.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
An amulet, often written on parchment

phrases.english: He said to him: As we learned:
Hide — enough to make an amulet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The measure is enough hide to make a קמיע.

steps.title: How much hide makes one liable for tanning? The same measure
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks about the measure for tanning hide, and רב נחמן says it is no different.
steps.simpleTranslation: [One who tans hide, how much? He said to him: It is no different.]
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks about a different מלאכה, tanning hide. רב נחמן answers that the measure is the same: enough for a קמיע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think tanning, as a separate מלאכה, has its own measure. רב נחמן says the same amount applies. The brackets show that this line is a textual addition found in some editions.

keyTerms.meaning: One who tans it (the מלאכה of מעבד)

steps.confusionAlert: This line appears in brackets because it is a textual addition in some printings. Do not confuse it with the next question (לעבדו), which asks about carrying hide in order to tan it.

phrases.english: [One who tans it — how much?
phrases.notes: The words in brackets show up only in some versions of the text.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is no different.]

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follow-up question about a different מלאכה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The שיעור for the מלאכה of tanning hide
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The same measure, enough for a קמיע

steps.title: Carrying raw hide in order to tan it: the same measure
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks about carrying hide that one plans to tan, and רב נחמן says the measure is no different.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he carries it out in order to tan it, how much? He said to him: It is no different.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks about carrying raw, untanned hide that the person intends to tan. רב נחמן says the measure is still enough for a קמיע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Raw hide is not yet usable for a קמיע, so one might think a larger amount is needed before carrying it counts. רב נחמן says no: because it is meant for tanning, it is measured like tanned hide. The גמרא will now look for a source for this.

phrases.english: To tan it — how much?
He said to him: It is no different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from tanning itself to carrying raw hide meant for tanning
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The שיעור for carrying raw hide intended for tanning
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The same as tanned hide: enough for a קמיע

steps.title: What is the source for this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source that raw hide meant for tanning has the same measure as tanned hide.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do you say this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a proof. It asks what source shows that hide meant for tanning is measured like tanned hide.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן's answer was not obvious, since raw hide cannot yet be used. The גמרא wants a parallel case where an unfinished material is measured by its finished form.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do you say this? (a request for a source)

phrases.english: And from where do you say this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a source for רב נחמן's answer
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that unfinished material is measured by its finished state

steps.title: The משנה about wool: whitening, combing, dyeing, and spinning use the same measure as weaving
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: the measure for working raw wool equals the measure for weaving spun thread.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: One who whitens, combs, dyes, or spins wool, the measure is double the width of the space between the fingers. And one who weaves two threads, the measure is double the width of the space between the fingers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה as its proof. Working raw wool and weaving finished thread have the exact same measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whitening, combing, and dyeing are done to raw wool, which is not yet thread. Even so, the משנה gives them the same שיעור as weaving spun thread. This suggests the raw material is measured by what it is going to become.

keyTerms.meaning: Double the full width of the gap between the forefinger and middle finger

phrases.english: As we learned:
One who whitens and one who combs
and one who dyes and one who spins —
its measure is double the full width of the finger-gap.
And one who weaves two threads —
its measure is double the full width of the finger-gap.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the requested source
steps.raayaObject: Unfinished material is measured by its finished form
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about wool: the work on raw wool has the same measure as weaving

steps.title: The inference: wool meant for spinning is measured like spun thread
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws the principle from the משנה: since the wool is meant to be spun, it is measured as spun thread.
steps.simpleTranslation: We see from this: since it stands to be spun, its measure is like spun thread.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the lesson of the wool משנה in a clear general principle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason raw wool shares the weaving measure is that it is designated for spinning. Its intended future state sets its שיעור now.

keyTerms.meaning: We see from this (introduces an inference)
Since it stands to (is designated for)

phrases.english: Evidently: since it stands to be spun —
its measure is like spun thread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extracts the principle from the quoted משנה
steps.raayaObject: Material designated for a later stage is measured by that later stage

steps.title: Applying it to hide: hide meant for tanning is measured like tanned hide
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא applies the wool principle to hide, which proves רב נחמן's answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too: since it stands to be tanned, its measure is like tanned hide.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the wool principle to hide. This proves רב נחמן's answer about carrying hide in order to tan it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as wool meant for spinning is measured as spun thread, hide meant for tanning is measured as tanned hide. So the measure is enough for a קמיע, the same as finished hide.
steps.whatToRemember: The key principle is כיון דלעבדו קאי — שיעורו כמעובד: material designated for a later stage is measured by that finished stage.

phrases.english: Here too, since it stands to be tanned —
its measure is like tanned hide.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the wool principle to hide
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Raw hide meant for tanning has the same שיעור for carrying as tanned hide.

steps.title: Carrying hide with no plan to tan it: still the same measure
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks about carrying hide that is not meant for tanning, and רב נחמן again says the measure is no different.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it is not meant for tanning, how much? He said to him: It is no different.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא returns to his questions and asks about hide that the person does not plan to tan. רב נחמן answers that this too has the same measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wool proof relied on the hide being designated for tanning, so one might expect hide without that plan to need a different amount. רב נחמן still rules 'לא שנא': the measure stays enough for a קמיע.

keyTerms.meaning: And not in order to tan it

steps.whatToRemember: In every case רבא asks about (carrying, tanning, carrying in order to tan, carrying with no plan to tan), רב נחמן gives the same measure for hide: enough to make a קמיע.

phrases.english: And not to tan it — how much?
He said to him: It is no different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבא's series of questions after the proof
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The שיעור for carrying hide with no intention of tanning
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The same measure, enough for a קמיע

steps.title: רבא challenges from soaked and unsoaked dyes
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks whether there is really no difference between processed and unprocessed material. He shows that soaked dye herbs have a smaller measure than unsoaked ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there really no difference between tanned and untanned? He challenged him: one who carries out soaked dye herbs is liable for enough to dye a small sample for a loom shuttle. But for herbs that are not soaked we learned: nutshells, pomegranate peels, safflower and madder have the measure needed to dye a small cloth for a hairnet opening!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב נחמן's rule from step 13. He brings a case where raw material and prepared material clearly have different measures.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Soaked herbs are dye that is ready to use, and their measure is tiny: enough for a shuttle sample. Raw, unsoaked herbs need a bigger amount: enough to dye a small cloth. That looks like proof that raw and processed materials do NOT share one measure.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged him from a source
Dye herbs already soaked in water and ready to use
A tiny dyed sample for a loom shuttle

phrases.english: And is there no difference between tanned
and untanned?
He challenged him: one who carries out soaked dye herbs
is liable for enough to dye with them a sample for a loom shuttle.
But for herbs that are not soaked we learned:
nutshells and pomegranate peels,
safflower and madder,

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי לִצְבּוֹעַ בָּהֶן בֶּגֶד קָטָן [לְפִי] סְבָכָה!
phrases.english: enough to dye with them a small cloth for the opening of a hairnet!
phrases.notes: A larger measure than the shuttle sample.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא שָׁנֵי בֵּין מְעוּבָּד לְשֶׁאֵינוֹ מְעוּבָּד? אֵיתִיבֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's answer in step 13 that the measure is the same.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's rule that raw and processed material share one measure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Dye herbs have a smaller measure when soaked (processed) than when unsoaked (raw), so the measures do differ.

steps.title: People do not soak dye for such a tiny amount
steps.stepSummary: The dye case has a special reason: nobody bothers soaking herbs just to dye a tiny shuttle sample.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it already said about this: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: because a person does not bother to soak herbs just to dye a sample for a loom shuttle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבא's challenge. The dye case is different for a practical reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference does not come from a rule that raw material gets a bigger measure. Raw herbs need a bigger amount because no one would go to the trouble of soaking herbs for so little. The general rule of step 13 stays standing.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was already said about this

phrases.english: But wasn't it said about this,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין אָדָם טוֹרֵחַ לִשְׁרוֹת סַמָּנִין
phrases.english: because a person does not bother to soak herbs
to dye with them a sample for a loom shuttle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the dye challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Special practical reason based on human behavior
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Raw material has a larger measure simply because it is raw.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dye measure differs only because people do not bother soaking herbs for so tiny an amount. The general rule stands.
steps.whyThisMatters: This line, 'אין אדם טורח', is the answer to every challenge in this section.

steps.title: Challenge from garden seeds before and after sowing
steps.stepSummary: Unsown seeds need less than a dried fig, or five seeds. But once sown, even one plant counts, as shown by the measure for manure.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what about garden seeds? Before they are sown we learned: garden seeds, less than a dried fig. רבי יהודה בן בתירא says: five. But after they are sown we learned: manure and fine sand, enough to fertilize one cabbage stalk, says רבי עקיבא. And the חכמים say: enough to fertilize one leek!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a second case where the measures seem to differ. Seeds before sowing need a bigger amount than a plant after sowing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before sowing, the measure is a group of seeds (five, or close to a dried fig). The manure measure is enough for one single plant, which shows that one sown plant matters. So the raw seed seems to need a bigger measure than the planted one.

keyTerms.meaning: The size of a dried fig

phrases.english: And what about garden seeds,
where before they are sown we learned:
garden seeds: less than a dried fig.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא אוֹמֵר: חֲמִשָּׁה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says: five.
But after they are sown we learned:
manure and fine sand:

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי לְזַבֵּל בּוֹ קֶלַח שֶׁל כְּרוּב,
phrases.english: enough to fertilize one cabbage stalk with it,
these are the words of Rabbi Akiva.
And the Sages say: enough to fertilize a leek!
phrases.notes: Either way, a single plant is enough to count.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge against the same rule, after the first was answered.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that raw and processed share one measure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Unsown seeds need several seeds' worth, while one sown plant is enough. So the measures differ.

steps.title: רב פפא: nobody carries one seed to plant
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that one plant counts once it is sown. Before sowing, a person does not bother carrying just one seed to plant.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it said about this: רב פפא said: this is where it is sown, that is where it is not sown, because a person does not bother to carry out one single seed for sowing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the seed challenge with the same idea as before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The larger measure for unsown seeds is not because raw seeds count less. People simply never carry out one seed for planting. Once a plant is already growing, one plant is worth caring for.

phrases.english: But wasn't it said about this,
Rav Pappa said:
this is where it is sown, that is where it is not sown —
because a person does not bother
to carry out one single seed for sowing.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא אִיתְּמַר עֲלַהּ, אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the seed challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Special practical reason based on human behavior
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Unsown seeds have a bigger measure because they are raw.
steps.terutzMaskana: The difference is only because no one carries out a single seed to plant.

steps.title: Challenge from clay before and after kneading
steps.stepSummary: Before kneading, the measure is a רביעית of waste water, which kneads a lot of clay. After kneading, the measure is only enough clay for a crucible opening.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what about clay? Before it is kneaded it was taught: the חכמים agree with רבי שמעון about one who carries waste water into the public domain, that its measure is a רביעית. And we asked: what is waste water good for? And רבי ירמיה said: to knead clay with it. But after it is kneaded it was taught: clay, enough to make the opening of a crucible!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a third case where the measures seem to differ, this time with clay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Waste water counts because it is used to knead clay, and its measure is a רביעית, which makes a large amount of clay. Ready clay counts with only a small amount, enough for a crucible opening. Again the raw stage seems to need more.

keyTerms.meaning: A quarter of a לוג, a liquid measure
The opening of a crucible where the bellows go in

phrases.english: And what about clay, where before it is kneaded it was taught:
the Sages agree with Rabbi Shimon
about one who carries waste water into the public domain
that its measure is a quarter-log,
and we asked about it: what is waste water good for?

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: לְגַבֵּל בָּהֶן אֶת הַטִּיט,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yirmeya said: to knead clay with it,
but after it is kneaded it was taught:
clay: enough to make the opening of a crucible!
phrases.notes: A small amount, much less than what a רביעית of water would knead.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third challenge against the same rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that raw and processed share one measure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The water for raw clay is measured by a large amount, while kneaded clay counts with a small amount.

steps.title: Nobody kneads clay just for a crucible opening
steps.stepSummary: Same answer: people do not knead clay only to make a crucible opening.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too it is as we said: because a person does not bother to knead clay just to make a crucible opening with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the clay challenge by pointing back to its earlier answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The water's bigger measure comes from how people act, not from a raw-versus-processed rule. Since all three challenges are answered this way, רב נחמן's rule stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: There too, it is as we said

steps.whatToRemember: Raw and processed materials share one measure. When a raw material seems to need more, it is because people do not bother preparing such a tiny amount (אין אדם טורח).

phrases.english: There too, it is as we said:
because a person does not bother
to knead clay
to make a crucible opening with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the clay challenge of step 18 using the answer from step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applying the same practical reason again
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Unkneaded clay material gets a bigger measure because it is raw.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is only because no one kneads clay for so tiny a use.

steps.title: עולא's three stages of hide, starting with raw מצה
steps.stepSummary: A new source is brought: עולא lists three stages of hide, מצה, חיפה and דיפתרא. מצה is completely raw hide.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי חייא בר אמי said in the name of עולא: there are three kinds of hide: מצה, חיפה and דיפתרא. מצה means what it sounds like: not salted, not treated with flour, and not treated with gallnuts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source (תא שמע) that it will use against רב נחמן's answer 'לא שנא' (steps 8 and 13). This step sets up that challenge by listing the three stages of tanning; the challenge itself comes in step 25.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מצה, like unleavened bread, means plain with nothing added. This hide is completely raw. The source will soon give a measure for each stage, which can show how raw hide is measured.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear, which introduces a proof
Hide at a middle stage of processing
Hide that is processed but not fully tanned
Salted / treated with flour / treated with gallnuts

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַמֵּי
phrases.english: Come and hear, for Rabbi Chiya bar Ami said
in the name of Ulla:
There are three kinds of hide:
matza, chifa and diftera.
Matza means what it sounds like,

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא מְלִיחַ וּדְלָא קְמִיחַ וּדְלָא עֲפִיץ.
phrases.english: not salted, not treated with flour, and not treated with gallnuts.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַמֵּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּעוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the challenges are answered, the גמרא brings a new source about the measure for hide.
steps.raayaObject: That unprocessed hide has a different carrying measure than processed hide, against רב נחמן's 'לא שנא'
steps.raayaSupportSource: עולא's teaching on the three stages of hide

steps.title: The measure for raw hide: enough to wrap a small weight
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the measure of raw מצה hide. A ברייתא answers: enough to wrap around a small weight.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much is its measure? רב שמואל בר רב יהודה taught: enough to wrap a small weight in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how big a piece of raw hide makes a person liable. It answers with a teaching of רב שמואל בר רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even completely raw hide has a real use, wrapping a small weight. So it gets its own measure based on that use.

phrases.english: And how much is its measure?

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yehuda taught:
enough to wrap a small weight in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the measure for the raw hide just defined in step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The measure for carrying raw מצה hide
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Enough to wrap a small weight

steps.title: אביי defines the small weight
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the small weight is a quarter of a quarter of a ליטרא, by the weights used in פומבדיתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much is that? אביי said: a quarter of a quarter of the פומבדיתא measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how big the 'small weight' is, and אביי gives the exact size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'small weight' is vague, so אביי ties it to a known local weight: one sixteenth of a ליטרא in פומבדיתא. This gives the raw-hide measure an exact size.

keyTerms.meaning: A quarter of a quarter, one sixteenth
פומבדיתא, a major Babylonian town with its own system of weights

phrases.english: And how much? Abaye said:
a quarter of a quarter by the Pumbedita measure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the 'small weight' mentioned in step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A quarter of a quarter of a ליטרא by the weights of פומבדיתא

steps.title: Defining חיפה Hide and Its Measure
steps.stepSummary: חיפה is hide that is salted but not floured and not treated with gallnuts. Its carrying measure is enough to make a קמיע (amulet), as the משנה says.
steps.simpleTranslation: חיפה is hide that was salted, but not treated with flour and not treated with gallnuts. How much is its measure? As the משנה taught: hide, enough to make an amulet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues עולא's list of hide stages. It explains the second stage, חיפה, and gives its measure for carrying on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each stage of hide is defined by which processing steps it has gone through: salt, flour, and gallnuts. חיפה has only been salted. Its measure is the one from our משנה, enough to make a קמיע, because salted hide is already usable for that purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: Hide that has been salted only, the second stage of processing
An amulet, a small written charm wrapped in hide

phrases.english: Chifa is hide that is salted
and not treated with flour, and not treated with gallnuts.
And how much is its measure?
As we learned in the Mishnah:
Hide: enough to make an amulet.
phrases.notes: This quotes our משנה's measure for hide.

steps.triggerLanguage: חִיפָּה — דִּמְלִיחַ וְלָא קְמִיחַ וְלָא עֲפִיץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the source from step 20. After raw מצה (steps 21-22), it now covers the second stage, חיפה.
steps.raayaObject: The measures for each stage of hide
steps.raayaSupportSource: עולא's three-stage list, with our משנה cited for the measure of חיפה

steps.title: Defining דיפתרא Hide and Its Measure
steps.stepSummary: דיפתרא is hide that is salted and floured but not treated with gallnuts. Its measure is enough to write a גט on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: דיפתרא is hide that was salted and treated with flour, but not treated with gallnuts. How much is its measure? Enough to write a bill of divorce on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes עולא's list with the third stage, דיפתרא. It gives that stage's carrying measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding flour makes the hide good enough to write on. So its measure is based on writing: enough room for a גט. The pattern is that each stage's measure matches what that stage is actually used for.

keyTerms.meaning: Hide that is salted and floured but not tanned with gallnuts, the third stage

steps.whatToRemember: There are three stages of hide. מצה is raw, and its measure is wrapping a small weight. חיפה is salted, and its measure is making an amulet. דיפתרא is salted and floured, and its measure is writing a גט.

phrases.english: Diftera is hide that is salted and treated with flour
and not treated with gallnuts.
And how much is its measure?
Enough to write a bill of divorce on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the three-stage list begun in step 20.
steps.raayaObject: The measures for each stage of hide

steps.title: Raw Hide Has a Different Measure Than Processed Hide
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא gave raw hide its own measure, wrapping a small weight. אביי sized that as a quarter of a quarter ליטרא. This does not match the amulet measure for hide.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, the ברייתא taught: enough to wrap a small weight. And אביי said: a quarter of a quarter of a ליטרא, by the weights of פומבדיתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now uses this source to raise a difficulty. The measure for hide before processing (wrapping a weight) is different from the measure after processing (an amulet).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the clay case in steps 18-19, the גמרא is testing whether the measure before processing matches the measure after processing. For hide, the sources seem to give two different measures. The words קתני מיהת tell us that the גמרא is taking the key point from the source it just brought.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, it teaches. This picks out the key point from a source.
A weight used on a scale

phrases.english: In any case, it teaches:
enough to wrap a small weight in it,
and Abaye said:
a quarter of a quarter of a litra of Pumbedita!
phrases.notes: This repeats the amount from steps 21-22, and now it's being used to raise the challenge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the raw-hide measure from steps 21-22 and sets it against the amulet measure in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling 'לא שנא' (steps 8 and 13): unprocessed hide has the same carrying measure as processed hide, enough for a קמיע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא gives raw hide a separate measure (wrapping a weight), not the amulet measure. So the measure before processing is different from the measure after.

steps.title: That Source Means Wet, Fresh Hide
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's weight-wrapping measure is about wet, freshly flayed hide. That hide is good only for wrapping, so it gets its own measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is talking about wet hide.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The ברייתא is describing a special case, hide that is still wet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wet hide that was just removed and left to dry cannot be used for an amulet. It can only be used to wrap a weight, so its measure follows that use. Hide that is on its way to normal processing keeps the amulet measure. The amulet rule still stands; wet hide is simply an exception.

keyTerms.meaning: Wet hide, freshly flayed and not yet processed (following רבינו חננאל)
There, meaning in that other source

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is saying wet hide is not 'hide.' It is still עור. It just has a different measure because it can only be used for wrapping.

phrases.english: There, it is referring to wet hide.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25 by limiting the ברייתא to a specific case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to a specific case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא gives the measure for all unprocessed hide, which would contradict the amulet measure.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא refers only to wet hide fit for wrapping. Ordinary hide keeps the amulet measure.

steps.title: A תוספתא Gives Hide a Much Larger Measure
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives size minimums for items to become impure through מדרס and מת: garment 3x3, sack 4x4, hide 5x5, mat 6x6. A תוספתא adds that the carrying measure for garment, sack and hide is the same as the טומאה measure. That would make hide's carrying measure 5x5, far bigger than an amulet.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in a משנה: a garment, three by three handbreadths, for מדרס. A sack, four by four. Hide, five by five. A mat, six by six. This is both for מדרס and for מת. And a תוספתא taught on it: for the garment, the sack and the hide, the measure for טומאה is the same as the measure for carrying out on שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a second challenge against the amulet measure for hide. It quotes a תוספתא saying that hide's carrying measure is five by five handbreadths.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה here is about the minimum sizes of materials that can become impure. The תוספתא then ties the carrying measure to those same sizes. That gives hide a carrying measure of 5x5 handbreadths, which clashes with our משנה's small amulet measure.

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity passed on when a זב or similar person treads, sits, or leans on an item
A sack, usually woven of goat hair
And it was taught about it, meaning a ברייתא or תוספתא commenting on a משנה
Carrying out from one domain to another on שבת

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a Mishnah:
a garment: three by three handbreadths, for impurity of treading;
a sack: four by four;
hide: five by five;
a mat: six by six;
both for impurity of treading and for impurity of a corpse.
And it was taught regarding it:
the garment, the sack, and the hide:
as is the measure for impurity,
so is the measure for carrying out!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge is resolved, a new source is brought against the amulet measure for hide.
steps.kashyaTarget: Our משנה's ruling that the carrying measure for hide is enough to make an amulet
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תוספתא makes the carrying measure equal to the טומאה measure, which is 5x5 handbreadths for hide. That is far larger than an amulet.

steps.title: That תוספתא Means קורטובלא Hide
steps.stepSummary: The תוספתא refers to קורטובלא, hide processed for covering things. It is not used for writing or amulets, so its measure is larger.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is referring to קורטובלא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second challenge. The תוספתא is talking about a specific kind of processed hide, not ordinary hide.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קורטובלא is processed in a way that makes it useless for writing or amulets. It is used for big jobs like covering vessels, so only a large piece counts as significant. Ordinary hide keeps the amulet measure from our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Hide processed for covering vessels and similar uses. It is not fit for writing (following the רמב"ם).

steps.whatToRemember: Hide's carrying measure follows its practical use. Ordinary hide is measured by an amulet. Wet, fresh hide is measured by wrapping a small weight. קורטובלא, used for covering, is measured at five by five handbreadths.
steps.whyThisMatters: Both answers on this amud use the same principle: a measure on שבת depends on what that material is realistically used for.

phrases.english: That is referring to kortovela.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27 by limiting the תוספתא to a specific type of hide.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to a specific case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תוספתא's 5x5 carrying measure applies to all hide, which would contradict the amulet measure.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 5x5 measure applies only to קורטובלא, which is used for covering. Ordinary hide stays at the amulet measure.
